name: x11-protocol-visualizer
description: X11 MITM proxy with live protocol visualization — inspect, link and throttle X11 traffic
author: Andrey Sidorov <andrey.sidorov@gmail.com>

comments.node-x11: The core decoder deliberately embeds its own span-aware reader with tables derived from node-x11's opcode values (see docs/decoder-and-state.md §2.1), so node-x11 is not a direct runtime dep. The npm package node-x11@1.0.4 also fails its native node-gyp build on Node 26; the current pure-JS node-x11 arrives transitively via react-x11 for the UI.
comments.@react-x11/components: Both UI packages come from npm (react-x11@2.9.2, @react-x11/components@0.7.0) and the peer ranges line up: components declares peer react-x11@^2.9.1, which our range resolves. The UI uses the composable <Tabs> family added in 0.4.0 (react-x11-components#50), plus <Table>, <Tree>, <Code> and <CodeEditor>. 0.7.0's breaking change is the removal of <DesktopCalendar>, which we do not import — the six entry points we do are code, code-editor, code-language, table, tabs and tree. Its visible change here is that <Table> and <Tree> now inset and round the selection wash, so a selected row reads as a pill on the list rather than a band across it; both committed screenshots moved with it. react-x11 2.9.2 is a fix for the native (Cocoa) <Button> and <Select> coming apart when a caller sizes them (react-x11#510) — which this app does, and only started to matter once the cocoa backend landed. The optional node-pty/@lydell/node-pty peers belong to the terminal component and stay uninstalled. @lezer/highlight is an optional peer <Code> uses for syntax highlighting; react-x11's remaining peers (@babel/core, react-refresh, hot-module-replacement) are optional and only needed for its dev-time HMR path.
comments.ui-optional: The react-x11 UI stack is in optionalDependencies: the proxy/decoder core installs and runs without it, and the CLI falls back to a headless console renderer (--record / --no-ui) when the UI can’t load. react and lucide-static are in there for the same reason — both are imported only by `src/ui`, and lucide-static is 61 MB of SVGs that a `--no-ui` user should not have to download. That leaves the core with no runtime dependencies at all, which is what the CI comment about the tests has always claimed.
comments.@react-x11/workbench: The component workshop (Storybook, for a toolkit with no browser): `npm run workbench` mounts the UI's own components from `stories/*.story.tsx` in isolation. A devDependency, not an optional one — it is never imported by anything the proxy ships, and `x11-workbench dev` needs a display. The stories import react-x11 through `src/ui`, so they are excluded from the core typecheck for the same reason `src/ui` is.
comments.build: The package ships compiled JS (`dist/`), not TypeScript. `bin/x11vis.mjs` imports `dist/cli.js`; `prepack` builds it, so `npm pack` and `npm publish` both produce a working tarball, and `prepublishOnly` gates a release on the typecheck and the test suite. Nothing at runtime needs tsx — 0.1.0 shipped raw `src/` behind a launcher that spawned `node_modules/.bin/tsx`, which no consumer install ever has.
